evals.query: We want our developer-tool landing page to feel like Vercel. The designer made it dark with a purple-to-blue gradient hero, glowing cards, and a neon accent on every section. Is this on the right track?
expected_behavior: Identifies this as the 'shallow imitation' of the aesthetic — copying a look without the system
Reframes toward a monochrome foundation: near-black #171717 (not pure #000), white, off-white canvas, hairline borders
States color should carry meaning, not decorate — drop the per-section neon and gradients
Recommends structure from 1px borders and tonal surfaces instead of glowing cards / heavy shadows
Emphasizes type and whitespace doing the work, with at most one purposeful accent
Does NOT simply approve the gradient/neon direction as 'Vercel-like'

evals.query: What exact colors, spacing, and border radius should I use to match the Geist design system for a product dashboard?
expected_behavior: Gives concrete tokens, not vibes: #171717 primary text, #ffffff/#fafafa backgrounds, #ebebeb hairline borders
Names Vercel Blue #006bff (current) and/or legacy #0070f3 as the accent for meaning
Cites the 4px spacing scale (4,8,12,16,24,32,40,64,96) and 8/16/32-40 rhythm
Gives the radius family (6px sm, 12px md, 16px lg, 9999px full) and the one-radius-per-view rule
References the 100-1000 semantic step model (backgrounds/borders/solid/text)
Pulls from references/geist-system.md rather than inventing an arbitrary scale

evals.query: Our app feels flat. I want to add some personality — animated gradient backgrounds, a bouncy loading mascot, and drop shadows on the cards to make them pop. Thoughts?
expected_behavior: Applies 'function over gimmick' — decoration that doesn't clarify structure/state/brand is noise
Pushes back on decorative motion; motion is for clarification only, ~150-300ms
Recommends borders and tonal surfaces over drop shadows for hierarchy
Suggests personality should come from typographic rigor, restraint, and craft, not added ornament
May note that 'flat' often means weak hierarchy — fix with weight/size/contrast, not decoration
Does NOT endorse the gradient/mascot/shadow additions as the fix

evals.query: I'm designing a logo for a small infra startup and want that clean, geometric Vercel feel. How should I approach it?
expected_behavior: Points to geometry-first: build from exact geometric primitives (the Vercel mark is an equilateral triangle)
Recommends monochrome — black mark on white, or inverted white-on-black roundel — no gradient or ornament
Advises against decorating the mark; precision and restraint over flourish
Connects to 'constraints are the design tool' — few primitives, used exactly
References visual-language.md geometry/triangle guidance
Does NOT suggest gradients, glows, or literal/illustrative logo treatments

evals.query: We have a hero shot that looks amazing in Figma, but the real app has dense tables, long names, and empty states. The team wants to ship based on the mockup. Good idea?
expected_behavior: Invokes 'design for real production usage, not a hero shot / portfolio screenshot'
Insists on designing every reachable state: full, dense, long-text, empty, light and dark
Frames craft as surviving the real product, not just the pretty frame
Warns that a flourish that only works in the mockup will fail in production
Recommends stress-testing the system's rhythm against real data before shipping
Does NOT approve shipping from the isolated mockup

evals.query: Pick fonts for our docs site. I was thinking a friendly humanist sans for headings and a different serif for body to add contrast and warmth. And we have a code-heavy site.
expected_behavior: Recommends a single grotesque family (Geist, or Inter as a free fallback) used precisely over a mixed pairing
Notes Geist is a Swiss/geometric grotesque with high x-height, built for crisp small-size rendering
Strongly recommends Geist Mono (or a clean monospace) for code, terminals, data, and technical metadata
Advises hierarchy from the type scale, weight, and tight display tracking — not from font variety
May reference the heading-/label-/copy- token families and 16px base
Does NOT endorse the humanist-sans + serif pairing as the right call for this aesthetic

evals.query: Accessibility review flagged that our minimal design uses #000 on #fff everywhere, removed focus outlines because they 'looked ugly,' and uses 13px and 7px gaps in places. How do we keep it minimal but fix this?
expected_behavior: Replaces pure #000 with near-black #171717 — softer and more considered, still high contrast
Insists focus outlines are part of the look, not a tax — restore a visible focus ring (e.g. the white-gap + 2px #006bff box-shadow) rather than removing it
Fixes off-grid spacing by snapping to the 4px scale (8/12/16...)
Frames accessibility and high contrast as native to the system, not opposed to minimalism
Keeps WCAG AA contrast as a requirement
Does NOT accept removing focus states for aesthetics

evals.query: I'm building a dark-theme dashboard in Geist. What are the exact background, text, border, and focus-ring values, and how do the 100-1000 color steps actually map to usage?
expected_behavior: Gives dark-theme anchors: background-100 #000000, primary text #ededed (not pure #fff), secondary #a0a0a0
Notes borders/overlays use translucent gray-alpha (e.g. gray-alpha-400 #ffffff24) rather than solid grays in dark
Gives the dark focus ring box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #000000, 0 0 0 4px #47a8ff (blue-900)
Explains the precise step model: 100/200/300 bg/hover/active, 400/500/600 border/hover/active, 700/800 solid fill, 900/1000 secondary/primary text
Distinguishes gray-* (opaque, for text/fills) from gray-alpha-* (translucent, for borders/overlays) and from background-*
Pulls exact values from geist-spec-dark.md rather than approximating, and notes accent blue is used for links/focus/success

evals.query: Review the copy in our UI: a button labeled 'OK', a success toast 'Successfully deleted the project!', and an empty state that just says 'No data'. Anything to change for the Vercel/Geist style?
expected_behavior: Replaces 'OK' with a verb+noun action label (e.g. 'Delete Project' / context-appropriate action)
Rewrites the toast to name the specific thing, drop the trailing period, and never say 'successfully': 'Project deleted'
Rewrites the empty state to point to the first action (e.g. 'No deployments yet. Push to your Git repository to create one.')
Notes Title Case for buttons/labels vs sentence case for body/toasts
Treats copy as part of the design — precise, no filler, no marketing superlatives
References the Voice & Content rules from the Geist spec

evals.query: Leadership keeps asking us to add more visual flair to stand out, but I admire how restrained Vercel's design is. How do I argue for restraint, and is it really just 'less is more'?
expected_behavior: Explains restraint as a system/engineering discipline, not a mood — strip every token that isn't carrying weight
Frames constraints as the design tool that makes remaining decisions meaningful, not a limitation
Notes the look is downstream of the system: build the system (monochrome default, borders, type rigor, grid) and the distinctive look follows
Connects 'simplicity, minimalism, speed' to a faster, clearer product, not just taste
Distinguishes the actual method from the cargo-culted aesthetic
Avoids reducing it to a glib 'less is more' platitude without the underlying discipline
